Explanation: The Fashion Listing is the Core Value Unit: a Seller-created offer combining the item, images, description, condition, price and style signals that Buyers can discover, like, message about and purchase.
eBay completed its acquisition of Depop on July 30, 2026. Depop continues to operate as a distinct brand, platform and customer experience within eBay.
Depop must grow second-hand fashion transactions while preserving the discovery, culture and peer-to-peer experience that differentiate it from general marketplaces.
More successful transactions increase marketplace fee, payment and boosting revenue while strengthening liquidity and network effects.
Depop must control fraud, counterfeit goods and off-platform leakage while avoiding the loss of cultural distinctiveness as it scales under eBay ownership.
Depop coordinates discovery, messaging, checkout, payment, protection, dispute handling and Seller payout around each transaction.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Order / Pay — Buyers place protected orders and pay through Depop checkout. | → Consumer · Discovery / Protect — Depop provides recommendations, search, messaging, checkout, support and Depop Protection for eligible purchases. | ← Provider · Listing / Fees — Sellers contribute Listings and may pay payment-processing, boosting or market-specific selling fees. | → Provider · Demand / Payout — Depop exposes Seller inventory to Buyer demand and coordinates Seller proceeds after transactions. | → Partner · Payment Instructions — Depop routes checkout, refund and payout instructions through its payment providers. | ← Partner · Processing / Status — Payment providers return authorization, settlement and risk status into Depop's transaction workflow.

Explanation: Depop governs prohibited items, counterfeit and dropshipping rules, honest listing content, community behavior and the requirement to keep protected transactions on-platform.
Depop grows demand through personalized discovery, search, app engagement, brand campaigns, creator culture and social media.
Depop operates recommendations and search, listings, messaging, checkout, payments, trust and safety, Buyer/Seller protection, boosting and Seller tools.
Its Buyer/Seller network, fashion listing corpus, social and recommendation data, brand identity and marketplace technology are core resources.
Buyers use Depop to discover second-hand fashion through a mix of search, recommendations, social signals and Seller profiles.
Buyers want affordable or distinctive fashion that fits their taste without relying only on conventional retail catalogs.
Depop combines accessibly priced second-hand fashion with individuality, discovery and the ability to buy from people whose style they follow.
Buyers face uncertainty around condition, authenticity, sizing, Seller reliability and whether an item will arrive as described.
Buyers purchase through Depop checkout using supported payment methods; eligible purchases receive Depop Protection.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Order / Pay — Buyers place protected orders and pay through Depop checkout. | ← Owner · Discovery / Protect — Depop provides recommendations, search, messaging, checkout, support and Depop Protection for eligible purchases. | → Provider · Offer / Review — Buyers send messages or offers and provide reviews after completed purchases. | ← Provider · Item / Response — Sellers respond to Buyers and supply the purchased fashion item. | → Partner · Funds / Credentials — Buyer payment instructions and funds are processed through the payment rails embedded in Depop checkout. | ← Partner · Auth / Refund — The payment rail confirms authorization and supports refunds when Depop initiates them.

Explanation: Access depends on account, payment and location support, while transactions and content must stay within Depop's marketplace rules.
Buyers access Depop primarily through its mobile app, with web access also available; 92% of 2025 GMS transacted on the app.
Buyers browse recommendations and search, follow Sellers, like items, message, make offers, purchase and review.
Buyers contribute purchasing power, fashion preferences, interaction data, social signals and feedback.
Sellers range from people clearing their wardrobes to high-volume resale shops. They create the supply, presentation and style context that make Depop's marketplace distinctive.
Sellers want to turn clothing they own or source into income while reaching Buyers who value their style and curation.
Depop provides marketplace demand, social discovery, Seller profiles and optional paid visibility through Boosted Listings.
Sellers compete for attention and must handle accurate listings, messaging, packing, shipping, disputes and Buyer expectations.
Sellers create the Listing and, after a sale, supply and ship the physical fashion item to the Buyer.

Explanation: Sellers must meet account and payment requirements and comply with Depop's prohibited-item, counterfeit, dropshipping and content rules.
Sellers list and manage inventory through the Depop app or web Selling Hub, with tools for offers, discounts, boosting, payments and shipping.
Sellers photograph and describe items, price them, respond to Buyers, negotiate, promote Listings and fulfil sold orders.
Sellers contribute the fashion item, original photos, product information, pricing, reputation, style and fulfilment effort.

Payment Processors are the strongest external complement to Depop's transaction model because every protected marketplace purchase depends on secure authorization and settlement. Depop Payments is powered by Stripe in the UK, US and Australia, while PayPal remains the payment rail for sellers outside those markets.
Payment Processors authorize Buyer payments, support risk and identity controls and move Seller proceeds through the marketplace transaction flow.
Depop's growing marketplace creates recurring transaction and payout volume for the payment rails supporting checkout.
C2C payments require fraud controls, identity verification, chargeback handling, regulatory compliance and reliable payout execution.
Processors authorize Buyer payments and settle eligible Seller proceeds, including fees and refunds routed through Depop's payment system.

Explanation: Participation depends on supported markets, payment methods, identity verification, bank or PayPal account eligibility and compliance requirements.
Payment infrastructure is embedded into checkout and Seller payout flows rather than presented as a separate marketplace destination.
Processors authorize transactions, manage payment risk, support refunds and transfer Seller payouts.
They contribute card and wallet connectivity, payment infrastructure, identity and fraud tooling, settlement systems and compliance capabilities.
